byline: By Hannah Beech, Karthik Patanjali, Evan Grothjan, Yuliya Parshina-Kottas, Niko Koppel, Miles Peyton, Jon Huang, Benjamin Wilhelm, Jeremy White, Jasmine C. Lee, Tim Wallace, Graham Roberts, Marcelle Hopkins and Josh Keller

contentUnits.title: Inside Tham Luang
contentUnits.text:
Step Inside the Thai Cave in Augmented Reality

By Hannah Beech, Karthik Patanjali, Evan Grothjan, Yuliya Parshina-Kottas, Niko Koppel, Miles Peyton, Jon Huang, Benjamin Wilhelm, Jeremy White, Jasmine C. Lee, Tim Wallace, Graham Roberts, Marcelle Hopkins and Josh Keller

Walk and crawl through the openings the rescuers confronted to reach the soccer team and their coach.

Experience the obstacles rescuers faced, like crawling through a two-foot opening, to get to the perch where the boys and their coach awaited escape. JULY 21, 2018

lifecycle.readerAction: Begin from a fixed, comfortable viewpoint before moving into the route.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The viewer faces the cutaway model, cover imagery and the route's cave entrance marker.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The headline, byline, metadata lead and captured interactive summary are preserved.

contentUnits.title: Light vanished
contentUnits.text:
Light vanished. Jagged rocks invited flesh wounds. Mud made every step treacherous. Monsoon rains poured in, turning crevices into muddy morasses and deluging entire passageways with rushing currents.

“You cannot let your mind slip out of focus, because when you start thinking, ‘I'm going to get stuck,’ that’s when you panic,” said Ruengrit Changkwanyuen, who trekked and dove through Tham Luang Cave to aid the search and rescue of 13 members of the Wild Boars youth soccer team who were trapped inside. “You cannot think about anything else besides the task at hand.”

lifecycle.readerAction: Read the hazard setup while the route marker leaves the entrance.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The cave route and profile panels frame the first description of darkness, mud, water and panic control.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The first two core body paragraphs are grouped without rewriting.

contentUnits.title: A mile and a half underground
contentUnits.text:
Mr. Ruengrit, a Thai manager for General Motors, rushed to the cave from Bangkok after seeing a television segment on the missing boys.

The rescuers, both civilian volunteers and Thai Navy SEALs, faced an overwhelming set of hazards. The path to the soccer team was largely uncharted, deep underground and a mile and a half long. One stretch was submerged in frigid floodwaters for the length of seven Olympic swimming pools.

lifecycle.readerAction: Follow the marker rather than moving physically through the cave.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The floor route and full cave map show the distance from the entrance toward the team.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The background paragraph and uncharted-path paragraph are preserved.

contentUnits.title: Stooping, climbing and crawling
contentUnits.text:
The point at which the cave first begins to narrow.

In another spot, near the entrance to the cave’s second chamber, Mr. Ruengrit had to climb and edge forward in a stoop. He scrambled down sheer, slick rocks. One misstep, and he could have fallen to his death. “It's a long way down,” he said.

From Chamber 2 to Chamber 3, he had to scale a precipitous muddy slope, alternating between a crouch and a crawl.

In the following section, explore life-size passages inside the cave.

lifecycle.readerAction: Use the map callout to connect the body text to the narrowing route.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The first source map callout appears while the cutaway stays centered at readable scale.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The first WebGL annotation and the chamber-climb paragraphs are preserved exactly.

contentUnits.title: Current like a waterfall
contentUnits.text:
He entered an underwater portion, facing a rushing current he compared to a waterfall. He had to plant his feet firmly or the current could have swept him away. And he had to position his head straight into the current, or the water would rip the mask off his face. At one point, he swam underwater for about an hour, in a 100 meter stretch near a fork in the cave. The murky, muddy water had “zero” visibility, he said. Even when Mr. Ruengrit put his hand in front of his facemask, he couldn't see anything at all.

Mr. Ruengrit said that even when he was wading through the water, the current was so fierce it was like a waterfall. He had to plant his feet firmly or the torrent of water could have swept him away. And when swimming underwater, he had to position his head straight into the current, or the water would rip the mask off his face.

At one point, he swam underwater for about an hour, in a 100-meter stretch near a fork in the cave. The murky silt-filled water had “zero” visibility, he said. Even when Mr. Ruengrit put his hand in front of his face mask, he couldn’t see anything at all.

lifecycle.readerAction: Inspect the human-scale model as the text explains current, mask force and zero visibility.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The diver-scale model replaces the cutaway while map panels keep the viewer oriented.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The underwater WebGL slide and matching body paragraphs are preserved.

contentUnits.title: Inch by inch
contentUnits.text:
This is near the T junction where divers first found the tunnel that led to the soccer team.

Instead, they worked their way forward, inch by inch, by touching the rock faces with their hands and tying guidelines to the stalagmites and stalactites. In the narrowest parts of the cave, rescuers detached their air tanks and approached a crevice feet first. To get through one fissure, Mr. Ruengrit had to approach at an angle and squirm through with his air tank held up by his head.

This is the smallest opening in the cave.

Instead, he and the other rescuers worked their way forward, inch by inch, by touching the rock faces with their hands and tying guidelines to the stalagmites and stalactites.

In the narrowest parts of the cave, rescuers detached their air tanks and wriggled through crevices feet first. To get through one fissure, Mr. Ruengrit had to approach at an angle and squirm through with his air tank held up by his head.

lifecycle.readerAction: Connect the source callouts to the guideline and crevice narration.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The T junction and smallest-opening callouts surround the diver-scale model.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The T junction, guideline and smallest-opening WebGL annotations are preserved with the related body paragraphs.

contentUnits.title: Where the boys were found
contentUnits.text:
In the deepest reaches of the cave, one underwater section stretched for roughly 350 meters. (Mr. Ruengrit did not go that far). On the other side, the rescuers discovered the 13 team members stranded on a rocky reach in small atrium above the water. They had survived in this space by licking the condensation from the limestone walls.

The cavern where the boys were found.

On the other side, the rescuers discovered the 13 team members stranded on a rocky reach in small atrium above the water. They had survived by licking the condensation from the limestone walls.

lifecycle.readerAction: Hold on the destination marker and read the survival detail in place.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The marker reaches the atrium while the final source map callout identifies the cavern.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The deepest-reaches and cavern WebGL annotations are preserved with the matching body paragraph.

contentUnits.title: Thunder, gear and endurance
contentUnits.text:
During the search and rescue, Mr. Ruengrit heard the thunderous sound of the water rumbling through the cave, as liquid filled air pockets and echoed through the Tham Luang complex.

Mr. Ruengrit said that the difficulty was not just the cave diving but also the hauling of heavy gear through the steep, slippery sections of the cave. Air tanks had to be constantly carried out to be refilled.

“Cave divers are a little bit crazy,” he said. “We do things that most people don’t want to do. It’s dark, it’s cold, it’s very narrow. But I like the feeling of adventure.”

lifecycle.readerAction: End with the physical labor and the cave diver's own explanation of why he kept going.
lifecycle.visualFocus: The route resolves at the atrium while the cutaway model returns as a whole-system view.
lifecycle.sourceTextPreservation: The final three body paragraphs are preserved as the closing beat.

spatialLayoutPlan.viewer: Fixed seated/standing viewpoint facing a low central model plinth.
spatialLayoutPlan.centralObject: The cutaway model or diver-scale model appears at the center depending on the beat.
spatialLayoutPlan.mapPanels: Left and right panels show the current source map, full route, cave profile or cover image.
spatialLayoutPlan.floorRoute: A low route line marks Entrance, Narrowing, Chambers 2-3, Floodwater, T junction and Atrium.
spatialLayoutPlan.xrPanels: Canvas story and notes panels appear only inside immersive sessions; desktop uses the HTML HUD.

opening.caption: Captured source imagery introduces the Tham Luang rescue and the article's AR premise.
opening.credit: Pongmanat Tasiri/EPA-EFE/Shutterstock and captured NYT assets

caveMap.caption: The source maps locate the entrance, chambers and long underground route to the boys.
caveMap.credit: Association Pyreneenne de Speleologie, Shepton Mallet Caving Club, Esri Thailand; via captured assets

narrowPoint.caption: A source map callout marks the first point where the cave begins to narrow.

tJunction.caption: The junction beat preserves the source callout where divers found the tunnel to the team.

smallestOpening.caption: The smallest opening is staged as a scale problem rather than a forced crawl in VR.
smallestOpening.credit: Captured NYT map and cover assets

cavern.caption: The final source callout marks the cavern where the boys were found.

cutaway.label: Tham Luang cutaway
cutaway.role: Captured cave cutaway GLB used to keep the route, chambers and choke points visible during guided narration.

diver.label: Rescuer scale model
diver.role: Captured diver/scale GLB used for human-scale beats about current, zero visibility and narrow openings.

controls: Advance and back through the guided beat sequence from desktop buttons or keyboard.
Controller select advances in WebXR; squeeze pauses ambient motion.
Desktop pointer drag rotates the active GLB for inspection.
Notes expose source mapping, asset roles and preservation decisions without adding required exploration.

transitionAndPacingPlan: Transitions move the floor marker and swap maps/models while the camera stays fixed.
Hazard beats slow down for reading and inspection; model swaps are short and readable.
No forced locomotion, crawl simulation, rapid darkness changes or underwater motion is used.
lifecycle.narrationAndTextPreservationPlan: The prototype preserves the headline, byline, metadata lead, interactive summary, all 15 core g-body story paragraphs and all seven unique WebGL slide annotations. Duplicate fallback paragraphs and unrelated NYTimes page furniture are excluded.

compatibility.sourceAdapter: Initial Web2VR per-story generated JSON instances.
